_note: Economy constants. Money is GBP millions per year unless noted; people are head counts.

population._note: People (Population.step_month, once a month). Each province grows by its nation's pop_growth (the scenario's yearly natural increase less emigration), less famine_decline times the share of food a nation lacks, and less occupation_decline a year while an enemy holds it. Soldiers killed (battle and attrition) leave the nation's provinces in proportion to their people, death_share of them. A province is never left under min_province.

tax_strain._note: What heavy taxes cost beyond the revenue drag. The strain is how far the rate is above the default toward the maximum, 0 to 1, squared. growth_penalty is taken off the yearly growth of the economy at full strain, support_penalty off the level war support settles at in peace, and war_weariness off war support each month at war.

labor._note: Factory output is multiplied by 1 - penalty times the share of the people under arms (never under floor). Peacetime armies cost a percent or two; a mass levy cripples the factories.

weariness._note: War weariness takes civilian factories for the people's goods: per_100k of all civilian factories for every 100,000 men lost so far (up to max). In peace it eases by ease_per_day.

starvation._note: A nation that needs imports and gets less than `below` of them through the blockade starves: factory output falls by `output` and war support by `support_per_day` each day.

construction._note: Construction capacity in IC (industrial capacity) a day. A nation has base_ic (small works everywhere) plus ic_per_factory for each civilian factory it holds that is not locked, less the people's consumer goods (the economy law's share) and the factories that pay for imports. A project costs `ic` and takes in at most its cost over `min_days` a day, so with ample capacity it still takes min_days, and with little it takes longer.

laws._note: Economy laws, from peace to total war, switched with the SetEconomyLaw command. consumer is the share of the civilian factories' work that goes to the people's goods and so is not available for construction; military multiplies the output of military factories (production lines); gdp multiplies the national output (the civilian economy is run down); weariness is lost from war support each month while at war. requires: war (the nation must be at war), mobilization (the least mobilization), war_or_mobilization (at war or that much mobilized). funding is the most the army and the navy may be funded under the law (1 is the usual upkeep; the least is funding_min); mobilization is the lowest and highest the nation may be mobilized under the law (a nation at war may always go up to the war floor of data/diplomacy.json); below the lowest it is raised a step a day, above the highest it is brought down at once. A higher law than the one in force can be taken only cooldown_days after the last change; a law whose requirements stop holding is dropped a step each month.

infrastructure._note: Infrastructure of a province: its railway level plus network_share of the best railway level among the neighbours the same nation owns, so a line of provinces with railways lifts all of them. Each point of it gives slots_per_level more building slots (rounded down) on top of the province's own slots.

factories._note: Factories are discrete. A civilian factory beyond the ones a province started with adds `output` GBP millions a year of industrial output (times the nation's development) to the economy and `income` GBP millions a year straight to the treasury (times development, the law's output figure and the workers left); one retooled to military takes both away, and the pool of construction points is what every civilian factory gives; a military factory makes equipment instead (phase 8). Each province has building slots: at least slot_min, one per slot_pop people, and room to grow by slot_growth over the factories it starts with. At the start each province holds as many factories as its industry is worth; military_factories of them are military: a nation's scenario figure, else its peacetime army over army_per_military_factory. A civilian factory turned military loses its output; the conversion costs convert_cost_share of a new factory and takes convert_days.

buildings._note: Province buildings. Everything costs IC (and flows of materials), no money. ic is the cost of the first level (a slot building costs the same each time); ic_growth raises the cost of each further level by that share of the previous one (0 = every level costs ic); min_days is the fewest days a project takes. materials are units of a resource consumed for each IC of progress (a flow: a shortage slows the project). Slot buildings take one of the province's slots and are limited to max_per_province. produces: units a day of a resource each one makes. consumes: kt a year per level. effects are fractional bonuses per level ('trade' is tariff income as a share of the province's output, lost to blockade). requires: 'coastal' needs a sea coast, 'capital' only the capital province. enabled false hides a building that waits for a later phase.

programs._note: National programs, switched on or off. Upkeep is a share of the nation's GDP per year. 'growth' adds to yearly economic growth.

resources._note: Resources, as flows. Figures are kt a year internally; one unit a day is 1,000 kt a year (units_per_kt 0.001), which is how the trade rates and the interface count them. deposits: the resource has a deposit table. stockpile: surplus is saved in a national stockpile (the others are flows: a surplus is lost or exported and a shortage bites at once). trade_rate: units a day one civilian factory buys. max_penalty: the share of what the resource powers that is lost when none of it is to be had. price is GBP a tonne (only the old money figures use it). industry_demand is kt used per GBP million of industrial output, pop_demand kt per inhabitant. shortage: output lost per unit of unmet demand (1.0 = all demand unmet).

flows._note: Daily resource flows (Flows). solve_every: the daily refresh solves them again only every this many days. min_trade_factories: the trade capacity (in civilian factories) every nation has at least, so tiny nations with no factories of their own can still buy what they lack. stockpile_days: how many days of demand a stockpiling resource may be saved up. overseas: units a day the world outside the map will sell to any nation with a coast (or a landlocked one with a friendly coastal neighbour) (shared among them, cut by the blockade; -1 is without limit). chem_per_industry: kt of chemicals a year per GBP million of industrial output times the nation's chemicals figure. chem_per_man: kt of chemicals a year the medical services use per man in service. animals_per_food: kt of draft animals a year per person a province's farmland feeds.
